author: sjgadler
text: The AI alignment problem seems likely to be *really* hard - thankful to @janleike @johnschulman2 and Jeff Wu for putting our approach more out-there in the world. Feedback welcome!

quoted.text: Our current roadmap for aligning AI starts with systems that learn from human feedback, uses AI to help humans give better feedback, and eventually involves building AI that can help us do better alignment research: https://t.co/YI0Oi5WQJi

author: sjgadler
text: Without tooling at their disposal, humans can only go so far in ensuring the robustness of AI systems. In the same spirit as our Critiques research, we want to give humans best-in-class AI to spot issues & ensure their intent is adhered to. https://t.co/fz7iiGT934

author: sjgadler
text: The way this works is that we generate a *batch* of variations at once, and by continuously re-selecting, you can move the image in the direction you want: like this version with a gleaming smile (which I didn't specify) https://t.co/zRPNWeSoo4

author: sjgadler
text:
Now, the left is pretty great IMO; it's a sharper picture and a bit less jarring. 

But I think most people's intuition is that "Variations = the same", not "Variations = a way to inject inspiration".

text: @patio11 @sama The goldfish one is tricky; even my adapted prompt doesn't do much better, nor do Variations on my favorite of it (the hallucinated text in the original here is very funny): https://t.co/HduE6uMaFr

author: sjgadler
text: @patio11 @sama Here's the Chicago one; at first, this wasn't recognizably Chicago, so I gave it a landmark and this came out a bit better; I then generated some Variations on my favorite: https://t.co/bbaA1YlpaS

author: sjgadler
text: Next, let's try to change the apple into another fruit - say, a bunch of red grapes. This is a bit hard, because the leaves in the original don't quite match what a bunch of grapes looks like. Nonetheless, DALL-E 2 is able to do it. I erase the apple's region, and get these back: https://t.co/gwP9N0Dya9

author: sjgadler
text: It might be fun to create some Variations on that image, so we aren't working from an *exact* copy. Here's what DALL-E 2 produces: Not bad! But I prefer the original, so let's stick with that. https://t.co/DXWBFNDFit

author: sjgadler
text: For those curious, I'll show an end-to-end process of creativing something fun. Art was never my strong suit, but with DALL-E 2, I can now "paint my imagination". Let's start with a classic like this: https://t.co/DJFEKlMGMc

author: sjgadler
text: Not all of these turn out with *great* quality; truthfully, I think I was a little sloppy with the region around the hand, and so sometimes we end up without a guitar at all. But, compared to the version that @ilyasut and I hacked together back in the day, I'll take it! https://t.co/2MBCrx46Ua

author: sjgadler
text: We start by erasing the region we'd like to inpaint, then give DALL-E 2 a caption to generate toward. With a little AI inspiration, we can give that old guitarist a shiny new neon pink electric guitar! https://t.co/wTT6zcz0gs https://t.co/VtDmDjMGth

author: sjgadler
text: DALL-E 2 can also make use of Inpainting, when an image isn't quite well-known enough to be generated de novo. Consider these attempts at generating The Old Guitarist by Picasso; they don't look quite like the original. Thankfully, we can edit the original if we wish! https://t.co/9LpAVnbXdr

author: sjgadler
text: With famous paintings, DALL-E 2 can often do in a single-shot what might have taken dozens before, and at significantly higher quality. Can you guess the caption for the below? (Ok, it's listed, but don't cheat!) https://t.co/DVx0uc8KY6

author: sjgadler
text: Once upon a time, we developed the technique called "Inpainting", which let you not only generate a novel image from text, but *edit* an existing image to look more like your caption. With painstaking iteration, it was possible to create images like the below. https://t.co/CPyJnDdmlT

author: sjgadler
text: DALL-E 2 is *leaps and bounds* better at image generation than its predecessor, which was already state-of-the-art. A thread with some notable comparisons: https://t.co/G9uYTdDUEa #dalle https://t.co/e2PFO3dBy0

author: sjgadler
text: @patio11 @sama @patio11 suggest some more and I can jump in too; this system is truly unbelievable, and such a privilege to work on
Check out this cool thing we made! https://t.co/Skw8jvYazS

author: sjgadler
text: We've learned a lot from deploying large-scale AI systems, and attempting to do so responsibly. Now, a bunch of colleagues and I have written up some reflections so they're in the public record and can help others more widely:

quoted.text:
Deploying and studying the real-world use of language models helps us learn more about safety and misuse than research alone.

As we advance our safety and policy work, we're sharing some of our findings to help others do the same. https://t.co/DcTDvAWxxD
